clue.text: Marine deserter cheers, coming round for one marine event

indicators.note: coming round says the first pair of words surround the next piece

parts.note: rats are said to desert a sinking ship, so a rat is the proverbial deserter at sea
for one means for example, abbreviated e.g.
ta is British informal thanks

explanation.surface: A sailor who has absconded is being cheered, perhaps as he comes back round.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading 'Marine' belongs to the deserter, not the definition: rats proverbially leave a sinking ship. Ta is British slang for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a series of boat races, a sporting occasion held on water.

clue.text: Give up new plan editor dismissed

indicators.note: dismissed says the editor is sent out of the longer word

parts.note: a redesign is a new plan

explanation.surface: Someone quits over a new plan after the editor is fired.
explanation.definitionFit: To resign is to quit or relinquish a post, surrendering it.

clue.text: Game, mostly very friendly, though grotesque

parts.note: Go is a board game

indicators.note: mostly says the friendly word loses its final letter

parts.note: thick, as in 'thick as thieves', means very friendly

explanation.surface: A sporting match that was cordial yet hideous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thick as thieves' explains thick for very friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: Gothic fiction is full of the macabre and bizarre, and grotesque describes the same strangeness.

clue.text: Matter sorted out by hospital specialism's medical intervention

indicators.note: sorted out says these letters are put into a new order

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: An issue settled by a hospital department's medical action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matter' reads as an issue but is simply the letters to be reordered; the department is ear, nose and throat.
explanation.definitionFit: Treatment is medical care given to a patient to cure an illness or injury.

clue.text: Story contributing to an out-of-this-world film

indicators.note: contributing to says the story goes into the word an

parts.note: a story is a lie, a fib

explanation.surface: A plot helping build a science-fiction movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Ridley Scott's 1979 film is titled Alien, and alien also means extraterrestrial.

clue.text: Majority accepting name applied to recent monarch of great significance

indicators.note: accepting says the first word takes the next letter inside it

parts.note: most means the majority
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen Elizabeth II

explanation.surface: Most people agree to apply a title to a modern monarch of real importance.
explanation.walkthrough: The recent monarch is Queen Elizabeth II, whose royal cipher is Elizabeth Regina; monster here is the informal adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Monster is used informally as an adjective for something huge or tremendously important.

clue.text: Marine SOS at sea — lots of rock formations?

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A marine sends a distress call while sailing among rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits masonry is stonework built by hand, here stretched to rock formations.
explanation.definitionFit: Masonry is built stonework, so many examples of it are piles of stone blocks.

clue.text: Prompt to overlook good sculpture?

indicators.note: to overlook says the good letter is left out

parts.note: to nudge is to prompt

explanation.surface: A reminder to ignore a fine statue.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is by example: a nude is one kind of sculpture.
explanation.definitionFit: A nude is an artwork showing an unclothed figure, a common subject in statues.

clue.text: Chariot out of control, source of claim regarding foot

indicators.note: a runaway chariot, its letters careering into a new order
source of says the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A runaway chariot is the origin of an insurance claim about someone's foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foot' is the metrical unit of verse, not the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: A trochee is a metrical foot of stressed then unstressed syllable, so the adjective concerns that verse unit.

clue.text: Sound from the bushes indicating rural crime

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the soft crackle of leaves moving
second meaning: stealing cattle or horses

explanation.walkthrough: A rustle in the undergrowth and the theft of livestock share one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaves make a whispering noise when disturbed, and stealing livestock is the countryside offence of the same name.

clue.text: French composer with obligation to follow it

parts.note: it is old slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA
a tie is a binding commitment

explanation.surface: A French musician feels duty-bound to come after something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to follow it' puts TIE after SA; 'it' meaning sex appeal is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Erik Satie was a French composer best known for the Gymnopédies.

clue.text: I note Star Wars villain appearing deceptive

parts.note: n. is the standard abbreviation for note, as in a footnote
Darth Sidious is the Sith name of Palpatine in Star Wars

explanation.surface: Someone comments that a Star Wars baddie is showing his duplicitous side.
explanation.walkthrough: Darth Sidious, the Emperor's Sith title, supplies most of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Insidious describes something harmful that works subtly and treacherously, beguiling its victims.

clue.text: Good stuff on radio, with sparkle

parts.note: radio content is listening, as in easy listening

explanation.surface: Praising some lively radio programming.
explanation.walkthrough: Radio output is called listening, as in 'easy listening'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something glistening shines and catches the light, so it has a sheen or shimmer.

clue.text: Pulse in dicky heart always lagging initially

indicators.note: initially says each of the four words before it gives its opening letter

explanation.surface: A medical note about an irregular heartbeat with a persistent delay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' looks like the heartbeat of the surface but means a lentil dish; dicky is British slang for unreliable or weak.
explanation.definitionFit: Dhal is a dish of split lentils or peas, and lentils are legumes known as pulses.

clue.text: Data novice working with it is switching off

indicators.note: working says these letters are being worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A beginner handling data is turning a system off.
explanation.definitionFit: Deactivation is the act of shutting down or disabling a device or system.

clue.text: Cold water movement having a severe impact

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
rippling is small waves moving across water

explanation.surface: Chilly waves on water hitting hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Crippling describes damage so serious it disables, as with crippling debts.

clue.text: A US lawyer taking care of variety of modern stars

indicators.note: taking care of means holding, so the pair surrounds the next piece

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, a US prosecutor

indicators.note: variety of says the following letters appear in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: An American attorney looks after a range of contemporary artists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stars' looks like celebrities to go with the lawyer, but means a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Andromeda is a constellation, and also the nearest large galaxy to our own.

clue.text: A little thing fades, going belly-up, then sadly gone

indicators.note: going belly-up means turning over, so the word reads backwards in this down entry

parts.note: dims means fades

indicators.note: sadly says these letters are arranged badly

explanation.surface: A small business fades, collapses, and is regretfully gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going belly-up' flips DIMS to SMID; 'sadly' rearranges GONE into GEON.
explanation.definitionFit: A smidgeon is a tiny amount, a very small bit of something.

clue.text: Ammo for archers falls out

definitions.meaning: first meaning: short bolts fired from a crossbow

explanation.walkthrough: 'falls out' reads as dropping, but it means argues.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossbow bolts have this name, and people who argue are said to have disagreements of the same name.

clue.text: Unionist made out an upward path?

indicators.note: out signals the letters are wrong, put back in a different order

explanation.surface: A Unionist politician discerned a way forward that led uphill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made out' looks like a phrase meaning discerned, but 'made' is fodder and 'out' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountainside is a slope of a peak, which a climbing route ascends.

clue.text: Indication of rank bovine material being linked to source of smell

indicators.note: being linked to says the smell's opening letter is joined directly onto the cow's stomach lining
source of says the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: tripe is the stomach lining of a cow

explanation.surface: A sign of rotten cow innards is a whiff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' looks like smelly, chiming with tripe and smell, but means military grade.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripe on a uniform sleeve marks a soldier's grade, such as a corporal's chevron.

clue.text: Mistake nearly all picked up over variable in astronomical model

indicators.note: over says the first piece sits above the next in this down entry
in this down entry, everything but the last letter of the mistake word is lifted to read upwards, the final letter staying put

parts.note: an error is a mistake
Y is a standard algebraic variable

explanation.surface: An error almost entirely caught above a changeable part of a planetarium model.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first four letters of ERROR turn upwards, giving ORRE, and the last R stays; Y sits below.
explanation.definitionFit: An orrery is a mechanical clockwork model of the solar system showing planets orbiting.

clue.text: Recalled some lack radiance — in this?

indicators.note: Recalled says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people remember being without light; the question asks where they were.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is semi-&lit: 'in this' points back to lacking radiance.
explanation.definitionFit: Darkness is the state of having no light, which is what lacking radiance means.

clue.text: Media manipulator backing rubbish and fake shots

indicators.note: backing says the three pieces in order are read from the end

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish
cod is British informal for mock or fake
nips are small drinks, shots of spirit

explanation.surface: A media fixer is supporting rubbish and doctored photographs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support, and 'shots' like photographs, but they are drinks read in the other direction. Cod meaning fake is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin doctor is a publicist who presents news in a favourable light for a politician or party.

clue.text: Hearing of a nobleman giving you time of day?

indicators.note: Hearing of says the word is as it would be heard spoken

parts.note: a knight is a titled man

explanation.surface: Listening to a lord bidding you a greeting at the right hour.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints at 'good night' or 'good day' as greetings a knight might give.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the dark period of the twenty-four hours, one part of the day cycle.

clue.text: Prod about masculine post

indicators.note: about says the first word goes round the next letter

parts.note: a jab is a prod

explanation.surface: Poke a manly mail delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post' is the upright of a door frame, not mail.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamb is the vertical side piece of a doorway or window frame.

clue.text: Boosting consumption blocked by tax cut

indicators.note: blocked by says the first word is obstructed by having the next piece put inside

parts.note: eating is consumption of food

indicators.note: cut says the tax word loses its last letter

parts.note: a levy is a tax

explanation.surface: Raising spending held back by a reduction in tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumption' suggests spending, as in consumer spending, but here it is the act of taking food.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevating means raising or lifting something up, which is what boosting does.

clue.text: Purpose of Elba, island no longer under French control?

indicators.note: under says the former-marker comes before the island in this across answer, the island riding on top of it

parts.note: ex means former, no longer
île is French for island, hence 'under French control'

explanation.surface: Elba, an island once ruled by France, served a historic purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: Napoleon was banished to Elba in 1814; 'under French control' tells you to give island in French, île.
explanation.definitionFit: Elba was where Napoleon was banished, so the island served as his place of banishment.

clue.text: Instinct to secure supplies for a horse

parts.note: a nose for something is an instinct for it
to bag is to secure or obtain

explanation.surface: A gut feeling about getting hold of provisions for a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosebag is a feed bag hung over a horse's head holding its fodder.

clue.text: People obstructing attempt to produce delicate work

indicators.note: obstructing says the first word stands in the way, placed inside the second

parts.note: a try is an attempt
a race is a people

explanation.surface: Some people get in the way of an effort to make fine craftsmanship.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracery is ornamental intersecting stonework in Gothic windows, or any fine lacy pattern.
